recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No follow-up source work is needed for FHIR-13575 unless PA later revises Appointment scheduling semantics more broadly.
issue_request: FHIR-13575 was a Published/Persuasive PA change request for STU3 asking that Appointment.requestedPeriod no longer imply minutesDuration must always be supplied, and instead clarify that duration could be provided but may be calculated by the scheduling system.
initial_application: No prior Issue-Reconcile-Key commit existed on the combined branch. Git history shows the Jira-era change was applied in 87ce43db922810cf7461a4b098916209234ae0be, whose subject includes GF#13575 and whose Appointment spreadsheet patch replaced the old mandatory-duration wording with the approved optional-duration wording; later source refactors preserved that text in current XML sources.
additional_context: Appointment is active in source/fhir.ini, so source/appointment/structuredefinition-Appointment.xml is in current build scope. The current StructureDefinition and the request mapping exception both carry the approved wording. Jira searches for the element and duration terms found only FHIR-13575, and Zulip/Confluence searches found no conflicting community record or later reversal.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current authoritative Appointment.requestedPeriod definition already says duration could be provided and may be calculated by the scheduling system, and the related mapping-exception source is consistent.
